newsitem.title: USA: Birmingham Steel forms scrap venture.
newsitem.headline: Birmingham Steel forms scrap venture.

text.p: Birmingham Steel Corp said it has agreed to form a joint venture with Mitsui & Co Ltd in southern California to collect, process and sell scrap.

The venture intends to use assets owned by the bankruptcy estate of Hiuka America Corp, Birmingham Steel said. The transaction is expected to close by year end. The purchase price and details of the transaction were not disclosed.

The parties are negotiating to purchase the assets, it noted, adding purchase is contingent upon completion of a definitive agreement, the receipt of regulatory and court approvals and final determination of issues with the Hiuka bankruptcy trustee and Hiuka's affiliates.

Affiliates of Birmingham Steel and Mitsui would each own a 50 percent interest in the venture, which would acquire assets of Hiuka located at Berth 118, Port of Long Beach, Calif., and operations in San Diego, Montebello and El Monte, Calif. The four facilities have an annual capacity to collect and process about 1.0 million short tons of scrap per year, Birmingham Steel said.
It said the venture plans to use the facility at the Port of Long Beach to export scrap.

"The joint venture will not only provide access to the scrap export markets, but could also serve to facilitate the export of other steel products. Also, the venture will be a potential source of scrap for the domestic market," Birmingham Steel said, adding "We believe that formation of this business relationship with Mitsui will provide the opportunity for the two companies to work together in the development of future strategic projects." -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
